data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 describes the flag as arising from a temporal misalignment between a 'sound and relevant' affirmation phase and a frontier-exclusion check, yielding both success and failure recorded for the same candidate. However, the adjudication-ritual standard (§11.3) is concerned with whether a sustained flag is legitimate under its own criteria. The claim of 'spurious' status is attributed purely to temporal ordering of internal critic phases, not to any actual substantive defect in the adjudication criteria themselves. Since 'sound and relevant' affirmations are issued before the frontier-exclusion check, the failure could be the substantive verdict; the prior affirmation does not render the failure spurious unless the ritual explicitly precludes failure after an affirmation. The artifact thus fails the audit standard because it conflates an implementation-time interleaving with a substantive adjudicative error, without establishing that the ritual forbids affirmations from being superseded by a later exclusion verdict.
